title: VideoAnalysis
description: Interpretation of one piece of content, anchored to a ContentEvidence object. Blocks carry different epistemic weight and a consumer must respect that: `deterministic` and `observations` may be used as fact, `hypotheses` may not, `unavailable_dimensions` says what was never seen, and `must_not_assume` lists inferences that are forbidden even though they look available. There is deliberately no separate downstream projection: an earlier draft carried one and roughly four fifths of it duplicated these blocks, which creates two sources for the same fact. Packaging output (title, hashtags, thumbnail) is absent by design; it belongs to create-script-and-packaging.

subject_state.description: Carried from the request because it is the single thing a downstream consumer most needs to know: whether this analysis describes the creator's own content or somebody else's. A third-party analysis may only be borrowed from at the mechanism level and carries must-differ obligations. Unknown preserves undeclared ownership, permits public-only observations and carries no owner metrics, baseline or source revisions.

evidence_ref.description: evidence_id of the ContentEvidence this analysis is built on. Media facts are read from there, not restated here.

content_ref.description: Minimum identity so a human can tell what this file is about without opening the evidence.

evidence_completeness.description: What the analysis could and could not see. A consumer must read this before trusting any dimension.

deterministic.description: Computed by rule, not by model: the same evidence and the same rule_version must yield the same verdict. Hook stage and sustain stage are reported separately because they were observed to rank the same two posts in opposite orders.

measures.description: More than one defensible derivation can exist for the same idea; all are reported and none is silently promoted. A measure that was already computed in the evidence object names it rather than restating its formula, so there is exactly one authority for how each number was produced.

source.description: evidence_derived means the formula, unit and denominator caveat live in ContentEvidence.derived and must be read from there.

evidence_ref.description: Name of the ContentEvidence.derived entry when source is evidence_derived.

composite_score.description: Fixed to null. Hook and sustain were observed to diverge, so a single scalar would destroy the only actionable distinction.

observations.description: Model-produced statements, usable as fact. Every entry must name what it looked at.

dimension.$comment: Kept identical to revisions[].target_dimension so an observation and the revision that answers it can be matched. `performance` covers statements about the metrics themselves rather than the content — an isolation run needed one and invented a value, and an earlier fixture had been forced to file a measured reach ratio as a hypothesis for want of it. `framing` covers where the camera is and whether the subject is inside the shot, which is distinct from `delivery` (how the person performs). One-frame-per-second sampling made runs of insert shots observable for the first time and four analyses independently invented a value for it; the precedent for adding rather than forcing a fit is `performance` above.

t_start_s.description: Only when the evidence itself carries time. A plain-text transcript cannot support a timestamp.

evidence_refs.description: Use this run's evidence identifiers: frame_id for frames, public_metrics.<exact native_name> or owner_metrics.<exact native_name> for metrics, and transcript.cue[i] for cues actually present. Preserve native_name verbatim, including dots; do not index metric arrays. Creator-view cards cite observations.<observation_id>.

unavailable_dimensions.description: Dimensions that could not be assessed, so that absence is visible rather than looking like a clean result.

hypotheses.description: NOT usable as fact. Unconfirmed explanations that go beyond what the evidence proves; a downstream consumer must not promote these into claims. Known evidence limits belong in limitations, and forbidden inferences in must_not_assume, rather than hypotheses.

revisions.description: Concrete changes the creator can act on. Required when subject_state is own_unpublished, because a draft review whose output is only description has not done its job (the product spec asks for specific rewrites here, and for improvements on published work). Optional for own_published, where a revision means 'do this differently next time'. Must be empty for unknown ownership. Conditional next-version mechanisms may be offered without asserting ownership or permission to modify this source. Must be empty for third_party: that video is not the creator's to change, and what carries over from it belongs in observations plus must_not_assume.

current_state.description: What the video does now, stated as an observation rather than a judgement.

proposed_change.description: Specific enough to act on without further interpretation.

evidence_refs.description: Frames or metrics that show the current state. A revision with no evidence is an opinion.

fix_stage.description: How expensive the change is. Meaningful only for an unpublished draft, where whether something can still be fixed in the edit decides if it is worth raising at all.

what_worked.description: Plain-language wins, each restating something already established in deterministic or observations.

edit_verdict.description: Keep / recut / replace for the next edit, derived deterministically by compose_video_analysis.py from what_worked and revisions[].fix_stage so hosts read data instead of re-deriving it from prose: keep = what_worked; recut = proposed_change of every revision whose fix_stage is not reshoot (a revision without fix_stage counts as recut and is counted in unstaged_revisions); replace = proposed_change of every reshoot revision.

must_not_assume.description: Inferences a consumer is not entitled to make from this analysis. Required, because the tempting wrong readings are specific to the evidence that was and was not collected.
